$comment: Expectations for scripts/check-export-coverage.ts — a RATCHET, not a config.
Every entry is a violation that exists on main today, with the reason it is
still there and the task that resolves it. An entry that is no longer needed
is itself a guard failure, so this list can only shrink. Written 2026-08-13
against the state before T1-T6 of docs/design/ecosystem-export-plan.md land;
the guard reads the live tables, so as T3 widens CAP_ENTITY_MAP the matching
entries here must be deleted in the same commit.
EMPTIED BY T3, 2026-08-13. All 44 unclassified capabilities are now decided in
packages/addon-provider-homeassistant/src/ha-export/entity-catalog.ts — 21 in
CAP_ENTITY_MAP, 23 in CAPS_NOT_EXPORTED with a written reason each — the dead
`siren` row is gone, and all 12 field waivers are resolved against the cap
status schemas that are their authority. The lists stay here, empty: they are
the ratchet, and the next entry added to one of them has to say why.
BOTH of T3's open decisions are ANSWERED by T9, 2026-08-14, and the notes they
replaced are deleted rather than left to read as still-true.
`intercom` IS exported: the cap declares `runtimeState: IntercomStatusSchema` and
the Reolink and Hikvision providers write it at the four points that open and
close a talk session, so the entity has a feed before it has a row. It is
read-only, and that is a property of talk-back (an audio stream a switch cannot
carry), not a missing route.
Tier A is no longer read-only: CAP_COMMAND_ROUTES names a route for every
writable entity — primary, extra and command button — across cover,
climate-control, fan-control, humidifier, water-heater, valve, vacuum-control,
lawn-mower-control, media-player, color, script-runner and automation-control.
What stays read-only stays so for a reason written where the row sits: a
vocabulary that lives on the slice (`availableFanModes`, `availableSources`, …)
cannot be a static `select`, and a setter that needs two values at once
(`setTargetRange`) cannot be two independent entities. The rule is unchanged and
is asserted BOTH WAYS by the catalog spec: a writable descriptor with no route
is a control that lies, and a route with no descriptor is an orphan that reads
as one.
`hapGenericTable` points at the HomeKit generic capability table; every cap it
names must be a real device-scoped cap. There is no coverage expectation for
HomeKit — the plan is explicit that HA's bridge covers the rows HomeKit skips,
so a cap absent from HAP_CAP_SERVICES is a choice, not a defect.
